newsitem.title: USA: IMF board approves targets for Argentine program.
newsitem.headline: IMF board approves targets for Argentine program.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund's executive board Wednesday approved changes proposed by Argentina to the economic targets originally set for a $1.2 billion standby program, an IMF spokesman said.
"After holding discussions this morning and early in the afternoon, the board members accepted the modifications," the spokesman said.

Argentina had requested a waiver in September, asking the IMF to allow it to end 1996 with a budget deficit of about $6.0 billion, up from the $2.5 billion shortfall it had pledged to meet when the loan was granted in April.

In 1997 the public sector deficit will have to shrink to $3.0 billion, which will not include a $1.5 billion charge Argentina's federal government will have to make for taking over provincial social security systems.
Regarding economic growth targets, Argentina will try to achieve a five percent rate next year, up from an estimated 2.5 percent in 1996.
In 1995 the Argentine GDP contracted 4.4 percent during a recession sparked by the Mexican peso crisis.
Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez has said that he will seek to start talks with the IMF later this year on a longer-term extended fund facility.
